tldr: By combining view-aware feature fusion with visual compression, RTPolicy compresses multi-camera visual inputs into just 12 tokens and uses 4-step flow matching to achieve both real-time inference over 30 Hz on edge devices and high manipulation accuracy.
hero_caption: Design concept, inference latency breakdown, and edge device performance comparison of RTPolicy. While existing methods suffer from high inference latency caused by heavy visual backbones and massive numbers of visual tokens, RTPolicy achieves dramatically lower latency and higher success rates simultaneously—even on edge platforms like the RDK S600—thanks to aggressive visual token reduction and 4-step flow generation.
overview:
In visuomotor policies where robots move their end-effectors based on visual inputs, action chunking—which outputs multi-step trajectories at once—has become the standard approach. In real-world environments, however, robots must frequently replan their trajectories (closed-loop control) using the latest camera frames to quickly correct deviations that accumulate during execution. Conventional models rely on massive visual backbones, huge numbers of visual tokens from multiple cameras, and dozens of iterative diffusion sampling steps. When deployed on low-power edge devices, their inference is far too slow to catch up with real-time corrections.

To address this, the authors developed RTPolicy, thoroughly streamlining the entire pipeline from visual encoding and multi-view aggregation to trajectory generation. Using a frozen lightweight DINOv3 ConvNeXt encoder paired with learnable view embeddings, RTPolicy exchanges dense spatial information across camera views and then drastically compresses tokens via residual downsampling and pooling. With these extremely compact visual tokens, it generates action trajectories via flow matching in just 4 steps.

In simulation across 50 tasks on RoboTwin 2.0, RTPolicy achieved a mean success rate of 52.26%, outperforming the strong baseline $\pi_{0}$. Furthermore, in real-world bimanual asynchronous streaming experiments, it reached a 72.0% success rate while sustaining high-speed real-time inference at 30.35 ms (32.9 Hz) on the ultra-compact edge board RDK S600.
contributions: Proposed RTPolicy, an end-to-end visuomotor policy tailored for edge inference by comprehensively eliminating bottlenecks across visual encoding, multi-view fusion, and trajectory generation.
Introduced view-aware feature fusion using learnable view embeddings alongside a visual compression module that slashes spatial tokens by a factor of 75.
Designed a flow-matching DiT action generator that outputs high-quality action chunks with only 4 Euler integration steps.
Demonstrated higher success rates and real-time inference speeds surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods across 50 tasks on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark and real-world bimanual manipulation tasks.

sections.heading: Why Do We Need Fast Multi-View Policies on the Edge?
sections.summary: Precise real-world manipulation demands closed-loop control that incorporates fresh camera frames to correct trajectory errors immediately. However, existing multi-view policies suffer from heavy vision and diffusion computation, making real-time execution on edge devices impractical.
sections.details:
To move smoothly and accurately from demonstration data, robots rely on action chunking—predicting and sequentially executing multi-step action trajectories—coupled with closed-loop control that continuously updates plans based on incoming sensor observations. In asynchronous inference setups where control loops and policy inference run in parallel, inference latency directly dictates how quickly the robot can reflect the latest visual scene into its trajectory.

Yet current visuomotor policies suffer from three major sources of computational overhead: heavy visual backbones used for feature extraction, an explosion of visual tokens caused by handling multiple cameras, and iterative diffusion sampling to recover actions from noise. For example, the visual encoder accounts for 52% of total inference time in VO-DP. Multi-camera methods like $\pi_{0.5}$ suffer from a token explosion that severely slows down downstream action models, while lightweight Diffusion Policy (DP) variants are often restricted to a single view and show lower success rates.

Here is the key idea: RTPolicy trims down all three bottlenecks—encoding, multi-view fusion, and action generation—simultaneously. By combining a frozen DINOv3 ConvNeXt encoder with aggressive token compression across camera views and a 4-step flow matching generator, it achieves unprecedented efficiency without losing critical spatial details.

sections.heading: Limitations of Prior Work and Where RTPolicy Fits
sections.summary: While many studies have accelerated trajectory prediction and diffusion sampling, few have optimized the visual fusion pipeline itself. RTPolicy approaches efficiency holistically from the underlying architecture.
sections.details:
### II-A Evolution and Challenges of Visuomotor Policies
Prominent approaches that map camera images and robot joint states directly to actions include ACT, which regresses trajectories using Transformers, and Diffusion Policy (DP), which captures multimodal behaviors with diffusion models. Recently, methods like RVT building 3D representations and VO-DP combining semantic and geometric features have boosted geometric reasoning. However, these improvements come at the expense of massive backbones and intricate geometry processing, making them extremely burdensome to deploy on edge hardware.

### II-B Efforts Toward Fast, Low-Latency Policies
To reduce trajectory generation computation, methods such as One-Step Diffusion Policy using distillation, FlowPolicy and ManiFlow based on flow matching, and FreqPolicy enforcing frequency consistency have been proposed. Other approaches like Streaming Flow output intermediate integration results on the fly. Nonetheless, these works focus solely on cutting the number of action generation steps; they leave the heavy upstream visual encoder and multi-camera fusion untouched.

In short, RTPolicy's strength lies in optimizing not just action generation, but the entire pipeline—from multi-view visual integration through token compression—at the architectural level.

sections.heading: RTPolicy Architecture: Balancing Speed and Precision
sections.summary: Images are encoded using a frozen DINOv3 backbone, enhanced with view embeddings, fused via cross-view attention, and then compressed 75-fold using residual pooling. Actions are generated with a 4-step flow-matching DiT head.
sections.details:
### III-A Problem Formulation
At control step $t$, the policy receives images from $V$ camera views $\{I_{t}^{(v)}\}_{v=1}^{V}$ and a history of past robot joint states $S_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{T_{o} \times d_{a}}$. It predicts a future joint trajectory chunk $A_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{H_{a} \times d_{a}}$, where $d_{a}$ represents the dimension of the state and action spaces.

### III-B View-Aware Fusion and Token Compression
First, dense feature maps $F_{t}^{(v)} \in \mathbb{R}^{P \times d_{v}}$ are extracted from each camera view using a frozen DINOv3 ConvNeXt encoder, where $P$ is the number of tokens per view and $d_{v}$ is the feature dimension.

- **View-Aware Feature Fusion**: To distinguish which camera each feature comes from, a learnable view embedding $e_{v}$ is added to the tokens of each view. Tokens are refined through intra-view Transformer blocks $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{intra}}$, concatenated across all views, and passed into cross-view Transformer blocks $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{cross}}$. This allows dense spatial features across cameras to interact and establish cross-view correspondence.
- **Visual Compression**: The fused features $\widetilde{F}_{t}^{(v)}$ are reshaped back into 2D grids and processed with residual downsampling and adaptive average pooling to compress each view into only $m$ tokens. In the real-world setup (3 camera views, $P=300$ tokens per view), 900 visual tokens are compressed down to just 12 tokens ($3 \times 4$ tokens, $C_{t} \in \mathbb{R}^{12 \times 1024}$). This represents a massive 75-fold token reduction.

### III-C Action Generation via Flow Matching
A Diffusion Transformer (DiT) acts as the action generator. The fixed robot state $S_{t}$ is concatenated with the noisy future action $Z_{\tau}$ and fed into the DiT alongside the flow time $\tau$ embedding. The 12 compressed visual tokens $C_{t}$ are injected through cross-attention.

Training uses Flow Matching, directly regressing a straight-line vector field from Gaussian noise toward the target action. At inference time, Euler numerical integration runs from $\tau=0$ to $\tau=1$ in just $K=4$ steps. Empirical results show that 4 steps provide ample accuracy, delivering smooth trajectories with minimal computational cost.

sections.heading: Strong Manipulation Performance on RoboTwin 2.0 Simulation
sections.summary: Evaluated across all 50 tasks in the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual benchmark, RTPolicy achieved a 52.3% mean success rate, significantly outperforming top baseline $\pi_{0}$. Ablations confirmed the critical necessity of each architectural component.
sections.details:
### IV-A Experimental Setup
Evaluations were conducted on the RoboTwin 2.0 dual-arm manipulation benchmark. Inputs consisted of three camera views (left wrist, right wrist, and head cameras at $240 \times 320$ resolution) and 14-dimensional robot joint states. The model was trained using only 50 official clean demonstrations per task and tested across 100 trials under the "clean2clean" protocol.

### IV-B Benchmark Results
Compared to official leaderboard baselines ($\pi_{0}$, RDT, ACT, DP), RTPolicy achieved the top score, with a 63.0% average on 10 representative tasks and 52.3% across all 50 tasks. It outperformed the strongest baseline $\pi_{0}$ (46.4% overall mean) by approximately 6 percentage points.

The performance margin was particularly pronounced on challenging tasks demanding millimeter-level alignment. For example, on clicking an alarm clock button (click alarmclock), RTPolicy achieved 76% versus 63% for $\pi_{0}$ and 32% for ACT. On hitting a block with a hammer (beat block hammer), it achieved 76% versus 43% for $\pi_{0}$.

### IV-C Ablation Studies
- **Impact of Demonstration Quantity**: Increasing demonstrations from 50 to 100 boosted success rates by over 20 points across all methods, but RTPolicy maintained a consistent lead over VO-DP and DP.
- **Integration Steps**: Evaluating flow-matching inference steps $K$ from 2 to 10 revealed that $K=4$ achieved an 81.4% success rate, matching or slightly exceeding 10 steps (78.6%), justifying the choice of 4 steps.
- **Effects of View Fusion and Token Compression**: Removing view-aware feature fusion dropped the average success rate from 84.4% to 78.0%, and removing both fusion and compression dropped it further to 75.4%. While token compression caused only a minor drop in low-resolution simulation (84.4% to 81.4%), it is the decisive factor for slashing latency when operating with high-resolution inputs on real hardware.

sections.heading: Real-World Bimanual Validation: Power of Asynchronous Streaming
sections.summary: In real-world experiments using two ROKAE AR5 arms, RTPolicy achieved an average success rate of 72.0% across three multi-stage tasks. Streaming control with concurrent inference and execution enabled swift correction of execution errors.
sections.details:
### V-A Hardware Setup and Task Design
The real-world robotic setup featured two 7-DoF ROKAE AR5 arms and three RealSense cameras (one head-mounted, two wrist-mounted at $480 \times 640$ resolution). Models were trained on 200 teleoperated demonstrations per task.

Three multi-phase tasks requiring high positioning accuracy were evaluated: (1) "Drag the drawer" (open drawer, place block inside, close drawer), (2) "Stack and cover" (stack two blocks and cover them with a cup), and (3) "Workpiece assembly" (place a mat on a base and insert parts into precise slots).

- **Streaming Deployment**: Policy inference runs asynchronously at 10 Hz alongside a 30 Hz robot control loop. Whenever a new action chunk arrives, an optimization problem considering acceleration and jerk is solved to stitch the new trajectory smoothly ($C^{2}$ continuous) onto the currently executing motion. This enables real-time trajectory updates with only one inference cycle of latency (within ~100 ms) without waiting for entire chunks to finish.

### V-B Real-World Evaluation Results
Across 50 trials per task, RTPolicy took first place in every task with an overall success rate of 72.0%, compared to 44.0% for $\pi_{0.5}$, 24.7% for VO-DP, and 4.0% for DP. On the highly demanding "Workpiece assembly" task, where DP failed completely and $\pi_{0.5}$ attained only 12%, RTPolicy achieved a 30% success rate.

Why did RTPolicy achieve such a large margin? The primary factor is low latency. Artificially lowering the inference frequency from 10 Hz to 5 Hz and 2 Hz caused the success rate to plummet from 94% down to 88% and 70%. Quickly fixing slight errors before transitioning to subsequent task phases is essential for real-world execution. Moreover, disabling visual compression in the real world caused the success rate to crater from 94% to 40%, proving that visual compression is vital for filtering out redundant background noise in high-resolution images.

sections.heading: Inference Latency on Edge Hardware: How Fast Is It?
sections.summary: Inference latency was benchmarked across four platforms: RTX 4090, Jetson Orin NX, and RDK S600/S100. RTPolicy achieved frame rates that vastly outperformed competing baselines on every device.
sections.details:
End-to-end latency from image input to action chunk output at batch size 1 was measured across both GPUs and low-power edge processors:

- **NVIDIA RTX 4090**: In FP32, RTPolicy operates at just 10.92 ms (91.6 Hz). This matches single-view DP while running 2.3× faster than VO-DP and 5.4× faster than $\pi_{0.5}$.
- **Jetson Orin NX (25W)**: On this standard embedded platform, RTPolicy recorded 143.2 ms (7.0 Hz) in FP32. While $\pi_{0.5}$ was too slow to be practical and VO-DP ran at only 2.4 Hz, RTPolicy retained practical interactive speeds within this low power budget.
- **RDK S600 (560 TOPS BPU)**: On this robotics inference accelerator board, RTPolicy clocked 18.59 ms (53.8 Hz) in INT8 and 30.35 ms (32.9 Hz) in INT16, easily exceeding 30 Hz real-time inference on an edge board alone.
- **RDK S100 (80 TOPS BPU)**: On this entry-level board, INT8 inference ran in 86.56 ms (11.6 Hz), successfully meeting the 10 Hz streaming inference threshold. While other multi-view policies dropped below 2 Hz, RTPolicy demonstrated exceptional adaptability.

sections.heading: Conclusion and Looking Forward
sections.summary: RTPolicy combines efficient visual fusion, token compression, and 4-step flow matching to deliver high manipulation precision and ultra-fast edge inference. While currently trained per task, extending this approach toward generalist models is an exciting next step.
sections.details:
This work introduced RTPolicy, a visuomotor policy combining a frozen DINOv3 ConvNeXt backbone, view-aware feature fusion, visual token compression, and a 4-step flow-matching DiT head. Rigorous testing in simulation and on a physical dual-arm robot demonstrated superior manipulation accuracy and real-time streaming inference at 32.9 Hz on edge processors.

A recognized limitation is that while visual representations leverage a self-supervised pretrained model, the action generator is fine-tuned individually on per-task demonstrations. It is not yet a generalist policy capable of executing diverse language instructions under a single set of weights. Future work will look into incorporating large-scale multi-robot datasets and task conditioning to expand RTPolicy into an edge-deployable generalist foundation model.

takeaways: In asynchronous streaming execution with action chunking, lower inference latency allows more frequent closed-loop corrections, directly driving up task success rates.
Multi-camera visual tokens can be compressed down to just 12 tokens without hurting manipulation accuracy, provided dense spatial cross-view attention is performed prior to downsampling.
Flow-matching trajectory generation requires only 4 Euler integration steps to reach high accuracy, dramatically slashing the iterative sampling cost typical of diffusion models.
Real-time multi-view visuomotor policies can run above 30 Hz on edge BPU boards like the RDK S600 without relying on expensive remote GPU servers.
limitations: Models must be trained and fine-tuned separately for each task, falling short of a unified generalist foundation model that handles diverse instructions with a single set of weights.
The robustness of the compressed token representation under larger camera counts or extreme visual occlusions has not been fully verified.
Because the visual encoder remains frozen, the backbone cannot adapt its internal features to fine-grained, manipulation-specific visual variations.
